newsitem.title: USA: National Steel to sell coke oven battery to DTE.
newsitem.headline: National Steel to sell coke oven battery to DTE.

text.p: National Steel Corp said Friday it has reached an agreement in principle to sell its coke oven battery and other related assets in River Rouge, Michigan to Edison energy Services Inc, a unit of DTE Energy.
National Steel said it expects to receive unrestricted proceeds of about $225 million from the sale.
The sale will result in an after-tax loss of about $25 million, but is expected to have a positive impact on future earnings, National Steel said.

About $157 million will be used to pay outstanding debt on the coke battery, which is a series of ovens designed to bake coal at 1,800 degrees to eliminate impurities and produce coke needed to make iron in blast furnaces, National Steel said.
The purchase is expected to provide Edison Energy with $100 million to $150 million in annual revenue from the sale of coke and coke byproducts, DTE said.

National Steel will continue to operate and maintain the facility under contract with an Edison Energy subsidiary which will own the coke battery, manage the venture and oversee the manufacture of coke and the processing and sale of byproducts.

A majority of the coke production will continue to be dedicated to meeting National Steel's iron-production requirements under a 12-year supply agreement, the companies said. An Edison Energy affiliate will manage the purchase and transportation of 1.3 million tons of coal annually to supply the coke battery.

The purchase is subject to the companies reaching final agreement on all aspects of the transaction, as well as customary regulatory review and the approval of both companies' boards of directors, the companies said.
